title: The Educated Barbarian: Meditations analysis (part. 6)
summary: Sixth Meditations reading: live as if time were short and do good, stop caring what others think, take inspiration without losing your path, shun fame and praise, do only necessary things, and the list of anti-stoic characters, from which he draws his educated barbarian ideal and views on masculinity and positive alphas.
claims: Having one life is not a license to do anything; it is a duty to be good each day you have
Detaching from others' perception is the biggest life hack: it frees huge time and mental energy
In middle school and early high school he was consumed by what others thought, which made his first months of high school hell
Take traits and habits from role models for your own life, but do not let each new hero pull you off your path
Fame and admirers harm you while alive: they drain you, and he has seen people close to their dream lose sight of it because of early fame
Write down your schedule, identify what is unnecessary and cut it; replace excess leisure with something productive like gardening
Hollywood's strong women just get the worst male traits; it is the balance of masculine and feminine virtues that matters
His ideal is to educate the mind and make savage the body: be as intelligent as possible with as brutish, muscular and strong a body as possible
Toxic masculinity is masculine traits unbalanced by mind and virtue; virtuous strong men are what protect the weak from savage men
A grown man who cannot cook, do laundry or hold a job is childish and needs to grow up
An alpha is a leader the group recognizes as beneficial; using power to keep others down disqualifies you as alpha and stoic
